entries.name: Apereo CAS
entries.use_for: Self-host enterprise single sign-on (CAS, SAML, OIDC, OAuth2)
entries.why: Long-standing SSO server used across universities and enterprises, supporting CAS, SAML2, OIDC, MFA and delegated auth.
entries.summary: Enterprise single sign-on and identity provider server in Java on Spring Boot. Supports CAS, SAML, OAuth2 and OpenID Connect protocols with multifactor authentication and delegated authentication; Apereo-managed, Apache 2.0.
entries.best_for: Universities and enterprises needing a mature, protocol-rich SSO server, especially CAS or SAML federation, on the JVM.
entries.not_for: Small apps wanting simple login, or teams without Java ops experience; it is configured by overlay builds and is a heavy server.

entries.name: Auth.js (NextAuth)
entries.use_for: Add OAuth, email and credentials sign-in to Next.js and other JS frameworks.
entries.why: Long-standing default for Next.js auth with many built-in providers and database adapters.
entries.summary: Auth.js: open-source authentication packages built on Web APIs for OAuth, OIDC, email/passwordless and passkeys across frameworks and runtimes, with database adapters or stateless sessions. The README says it is now part of Better Auth and recommends Better Auth for new projects.
entries.best_for: Existing Next.js and other JS apps already using Auth.js, or stateless session setups without a database.
entries.not_for: New projects, where the README recommends Better Auth unless you need a specific gap such as stateless sessions. Not a hosted identity service.

entries.name: Authelia
entries.use_for: SSO and multi-factor portal that protects apps behind a reverse proxy.
entries.why: OpenID Certified, lightweight and popular for self-hosted setups.
entries.summary: Authentication and authorization server giving two-factor auth and SSO via a web portal. Works with reverse proxies to allow, deny or redirect requests; supports OpenID Connect 1.0/OAuth 2.0, WebAuthn, TOTP and more, deployed as a binary, package, Docker or Helm chart.
entries.best_for: Protecting self-hosted apps behind nginx, Traefik or similar with MFA and SSO.
entries.not_for: Apps needing in-app user management or SDK-based login flows; it is a portal and companion to a reverse proxy, not a full user directory.

entries.name: authentik
entries.use_for: Self-hosted identity provider with SSO, OIDC, SAML, LDAP and proxy auth
entries.why: Popular self-hosted IdP alternative to Okta/Keycloak

license_verified.note: MIT core; authentik/enterprise/ under its own enterprise license, website/ CC BY-SA 4.0

entries.summary: Open-source identity provider for SSO supporting SAML, OAuth2/OIDC, LDAP, RADIUS and more. Designed for self-hosting from small labs to large clusters; an enterprise offering exists.
entries.best_for: Self-hosted SSO for many internal apps with a polished admin UI, as an Okta or Auth0 alternative.
entries.not_for: Small apps that only need login library code; it is a multi-service server to run. Some features are enterprise-licensed.

entries.name: Authlib
entries.use_for: Build OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect clients and servers in Python.
entries.why: Spec-complete library with integrations for Flask, Django, FastAPI and httpx.
entries.summary: Python library for building OAuth 1.0/2.0 and OpenID Connect clients and servers, including JWS, JWK, JWA and JWT. Implements many RFCs (PKCE, token introspection and revocation, device grant, dynamic client registration) with Flask, Django, FastAPI and httpx integrations.
entries.best_for: Python projects that need to be an OAuth/OIDC provider or consume OAuth APIs with spec-compliant code.
entries.not_for: Turnkey login UI or user management; it is a protocol toolkit you assemble yourself, not an identity server.

entries.name: Better Auth
entries.use_for: Framework-agnostic TypeScript auth with email/password, OAuth, 2FA, orgs and plugins.
entries.why: Fast-growing, comprehensive self-hosted auth for TS apps; user data stays in your own database.
entries.summary: Framework-agnostic TypeScript authentication and authorization framework with a plugin ecosystem. Provides email/password, OAuth, 2FA, multi-tenant/organizations and other features, storing data in your own database.
entries.best_for: TypeScript apps (Next.js, Nuxt, Hono, etc.) that want comprehensive self-hosted auth with 2FA and organizations.
entries.not_for: Non-TypeScript backends, or teams who prefer a fully hosted identity service; you own the database and operations.

entries.name: Casbin
entries.use_for: Authorization library supporting ACL, RBAC and ABAC models.
entries.why: Language-portable policy engine with ports for Node, Python, Java and more.
entries.summary: Access-control library for Go enforcing ACL, RBAC and ABAC. Models are defined in a PERM (Policy, Effect, Request, Matchers) config file, so switching models means editing configuration; ports exist for other languages.
entries.best_for: Adding role- or attribute-based permission checks to an app with policies stored in files or databases.
entries.not_for: Authentication or user management; it only decides authorization. Policy model design takes learning, and other-language ports vary in maturity.

entries.name: Casdoor
entries.use_for: UI-first IAM / SSO platform with OAuth, OIDC, SAML and LDAP
entries.why: Popular open-source IAM from the Casbin org
entries.summary: UI-first identity and access management server with an admin console. Handles SSO, OAuth, OIDC, SAML, LDAP, WebAuthn, social providers and multiple organizations/applications, issuing tokens so apps never handle passwords.
entries.best_for: Self-hosting a complete IdP with web console for user, app and provider management, from the Casbin org.
entries.not_for: Embedding auth as a library, or very large enterprises needing deep audit/compliance tooling; it is a standalone server to operate.

entries.name: Clerk JavaScript SDKs
entries.use_for: Official SDKs for Clerk hosted auth: drop-in sign-in, user and organization components.
entries.why: Fastest path to polished auth UI if a hosted service is acceptable; official vendor repo.
entries.summary: Official SDKs for Clerk, a hosted user-management service. Provides drop-in sign-in/sign-up components, user profile and organization UI, with packages like @clerk/nextjs for frameworks.
entries.best_for: Fastest path to polished auth UI with a managed service in Next.js, React and other JS frameworks.
entries.not_for: Self-hosting or keeping user data on your own infrastructure; the SDKs require a Clerk account and the hosted service is paid beyond limits.

entries.name: Devise
entries.use_for: Flexible authentication for Rails apps.
entries.why: The standard Rails authentication gem with a large extension ecosystem.
entries.summary: Modular authentication solution for Rails based on Warden and Rails engines. Ten modules include database authenticatable, omniauthable, confirmable, recoverable, registerable, rememberable, trackable, timeoutable, validatable and lockable; supports multiple models signed in at once.
entries.best_for: Rails apps needing standard email/password accounts, confirmation, recovery and OmniAuth login.
entries.not_for: Non-Rails stacks, API-only token auth without add-ons, or modern passwordless/passkey flows out of the box. Customization can be heavy.

entries.name: django-allauth
entries.use_for: Authentication, registration, social login and MFA for Django.
entries.why: The go-to Django auth package with many social providers.
entries.summary: django-allauth is an integrated set of Django apps for authentication, registration, account management and social login. It handles local login by username or email with configurable email verification, plus OpenID Connect, OAuth 1.0/2.0 and SAML 2.0 providers. Rate limiting and account-enumeration prevention are on by default, and behaviour is customised via an adapter pattern.
entries.best_for: Django projects that need local accounts and social or enterprise SSO (OIDC, OAuth, SAML) in one package, including email verification and rate limiting.
entries.not_for: Non-Django stacks. Development has moved to Codeberg, so the GitHub repo is a mirror for issues and source. Overkill if you only need Django's built-in username/password login.

entries.name: jose
entries.use_for: JWT, JWS, JWE and JWK for every JS runtime
entries.why: Most used universal JWT library; used by Auth.js and others
entries.summary: Universal JavaScript module for JOSE: JWT, JWS, JWE, JWK and JWKS. Runs on Node.js, browsers, Cloudflare Workers, Deno and Bun using Web APIs.
entries.best_for: Signing, verifying and encrypting JWTs and handling JWKS across any JS runtime, including edge.
entries.not_for: Full authentication or session management; it provides only token and crypto primitives. Not a replacement for an auth framework.

entries.name: Keycloak
entries.use_for: Self-hosted identity and access management with SSO, OIDC, SAML and user federation.
entries.why: CNCF project and the most widely deployed open-source IAM server.
entries.summary: Open-source identity and access management server: SSO, user federation, strong authentication, user management and fine-grained authorization. Start with the distribution or Docker image (start-dev); CNCF project.
entries.best_for: Self-hosted enterprise IAM with OIDC/SAML, LDAP federation and many clients.
entries.not_for: Small apps, where its JVM footprint and admin complexity are overkill; a library like Better Auth or a hosted service is simpler.

entries.name: Logto
entries.use_for: Auth and authorization infrastructure for SaaS and AI apps, built on OIDC.
entries.why: Developer-friendly Auth0 alternative with organizations, RBAC and many SDKs.
entries.summary: Open-source auth infrastructure built on OIDC and OAuth 2.1, with multi-tenancy, enterprise SSO, RBAC, pre-built customizable sign-in flows and SDKs for 30+ frameworks. Also targets MCP and agent-based AI apps; available as Logto Cloud or self-hosted.
entries.best_for: SaaS products needing organizations, enterprise SSO and RBAC with quick SDK integration, as an Auth0 alternative.
entries.not_for: Apps that only need a lightweight library, or teams unwilling to run a separate identity service (or pay for cloud).

entries.name: node-oidc-provider
entries.use_for: Build an OpenID-certified OAuth 2.0 / OIDC provider in Node
entries.why: Certified OIDC provider library used by many IdPs
entries.summary: Node.js library implementing an OAuth 2.0 authorization server with OpenID Connect and many additional specs (discovery, dynamic registration, PAR, DPoP, etc.). OpenID certified; features are configured and not all enabled by default.
entries.best_for: Building a custom, standards-certified OIDC provider in Node with full control over UI and storage.
entries.not_for: Out-of-box login UI or user management; you implement interaction, accounts and persistence. Use Keycloak, Logto or Ory for turnkey servers.

entries.name: OAuth2 Proxy
entries.use_for: Put OAuth2/OIDC login in front of any web app
entries.why: Standard way to protect internal apps behind SSO
entries.summary: Reverse proxy and middleware that adds OAuth2/OIDC authentication in front of web apps. Supports generic OIDC plus providers like Google, Microsoft Entra ID, GitHub and login.gov, and integrates with existing reverse proxies or load balancers.
entries.best_for: Quickly protecting internal tools or apps with SSO login without changing app code.
entries.not_for: Fine-grained authorization or user management inside the app; it authenticates requests but does not manage users or permissions.

entries.name: Ory Hydra
entries.use_for: Certified OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect server
entries.why: OpenID-certified OAuth2 provider; complements Ory Kratos
entries.summary: OpenID-certified OAuth 2.0 server and OpenID Connect provider optimized for low latency and throughput. It delegates login and consent to your own app, so it does not store users and gives you full UI control.
entries.best_for: Issuing OAuth2/OIDC tokens for your own identity system, often paired with Ory Kratos.
entries.not_for: Turnkey login with user management; you must build the login/consent app. Not for projects that only need simple sessions.

entries.name: Ory Kratos
entries.use_for: Headless, API-first identity and user management server (login, registration, MFA, recovery).
entries.why: Cloud-native, bring-your-own-UI identity server; part of the Ory stack with Hydra for OAuth2.
entries.summary: Headless, API-first identity and user management server handling self-service login, registration, account verification and recovery, multi-factor authentication and profile management. You bring your own UI; works alongside Ory Hydra for OAuth2; self-host or Ory Network.
entries.best_for: Cloud-native apps wanting full control of auth UX with a dedicated identity service.
entries.not_for: Out-of-the-box UI or monolithic apps wanting a drop-in library; you build the frontend flows and run another service.

entries.name: SimpleWebAuthn
entries.use_for: Add passkeys/WebAuthn to TS apps with server and browser helpers
entries.why: Most used WebAuthn library for JS
entries.summary: Two TypeScript libraries, @simplewebauthn/server and @simplewebauthn/browser, that reduce the work of adding WebAuthn/passkeys to a website. Includes an example Express project.
entries.best_for: Adding passkey registration and login to a JS/TS backend and frontend.
entries.not_for: Full user management or sessions; it only handles WebAuthn ceremonies. Non-JS backends need another library.

entries.name: SuperTokens
entries.use_for: Self-hostable auth with sessions, passwordless and social login
entries.why: Open-source alternative to Auth0/Firebase Auth with SDKs

license_verified.note: Apache-2.0 outside ee/; ee/ under its own enterprise license

entries.summary: Open-source auth with passwordless, social login, email/password and session management. Architecture has a frontend SDK, a backend SDK exposing auth APIs, and a core HTTP service handling logic and database operations; SDKs for Node, Go, Python and React.
entries.best_for: Self-hostable auth with prebuilt UI and sessions as an alternative to Auth0 or Firebase Auth.
entries.not_for: Teams that want a single library with no extra service; the core is a separate component to deploy, and some features are paid.

entries.name: ZITADEL
entries.use_for: Identity infrastructure with multi-tenancy, OIDC/SAML, passkeys and audit trail.
entries.why: Strong multi-tenant B2B support; self-host or use the cloud. AGPL-3.0.
entries.summary: Open-source identity and access management platform with SSO, MFA, passkeys, OIDC, SAML, SCIM and a multi-tenancy model, plus an audit trail. API-first; self-host or use the cloud. AGPL-3.0.
entries.best_for: B2B SaaS needing strong multi-tenant identity, with the option to self-host.
entries.not_for: Small apps or teams with license concerns: it is AGPL-3.0 and a larger platform to operate.
